findings.F1: The 24-hour reversal is not special to weekends: on a non-overlapping daily grid of every day, the drift-adjusted next-24h return regressed on the past 24h return in usual 30-day moves has a slope of -0.00168 (t -5.85, 12638 cases). By the weekday of the closing day, the next-24h slope is -0.0036 (t -3.9) at Monday 00:00 but just as large on other days: -0.0034 (t -4.6) at Sunday 00:00, -0.0024 (t -4.1) on Friday and -0.0027 (t -3.8) on Thursday. Tuesday's slope is the only positive one (+0.0017, t 2.8).
findings.F2: That reversal grows with volatility. When the coin's 30-day usual move is measured against its own median over about 83 days, the daily-grid slope is +0.0004 (t 0.9) in the low tercile, -0.0023 (t -4.5) in the middle and -0.0032 (t -6.3) in the high tercile. The z × vol-ratio interaction is -0.0029 (t -3.6). In the high-vol tercile the next-24h return is +0.66 % after the lowest third of 24h moves and -0.25 % after the highest third, a spread of about 0.9 %. That spread is 4.8 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. The high-vol slope is negative in all 8 years (t from -0.9 to -4.7) and in every coin, with t below -2 everywhere except XRP (t -1.1).
findings.F3: The tested Monday effect sits almost wholly in high volatility. The Monday 48h slope is -0.0119 (t -4.8, 598 cases) in the high vol tercile, -0.0021 (t -0.9) in the middle and +0.0033 (t 1.3) in the low tercile. By coin it is only t -0.7 to -2.0 (about 375 cases each), and by year only 2019, 2020 and 2025 have t below -2.
findings.F4: The Monday response is not graded at the top. By Sunday-move quintile the next-48h drift-adjusted return is +0.98 %, +0.13 %, -0.48 %, -1.36 % and -0.40 % at mean z of -1.56, -0.50, 0.02, 0.54 and 1.70. The largest Sunday rises reverse less than moderate ones.
findings.F5: The book earns on Mondays only. Its mean daily return is +0.095 % on Mondays, +0.022 % on Tuesdays and between -0.039 % and +0.003 % on the other five days (about 2480 coin-days each). This fits a position opened at Monday 00:00 that carries little after its first day.
findings.F6: The two hours closing at 23:00 UTC (the 21:00 and 22:00 UTC hourly bars) rise on average by +0.097 % (t 9.1, 17403 cases). The rise is positive in 7 of 8 years (2022 is -0.04 %), in every coin (t 3.1 to 4.7) and on every weekday (t 2.1 to 4.4). It is larger in high volatility (+0.144 %, t 6.2) than in low volatility (+0.071 %, t 3.6). It is also larger after a 24h fall (+0.144 % in the lowest third of prior z, against +0.079 % in the highest; slope on z t -3.3). Even in high volatility the move is below the 0.19 % cost of a trade.

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return, measured in its usual 30-day move, is followed over the next 24 hours by a move in the opposite direction, on any day of the week. The larger that return and the higher the coin's current 30-day usual move against its own usual level of the past three months, the larger the reversal.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean against the past day's move every day rather than only on Mondays, and bet more when the coin is unusually volatile.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled daily reversal

ideas.idea: A coin's Sunday 24-hour return, measured in its usual 30-day move, is reversed over Monday and Tuesday by more the higher the coin's current 30-day usual move stands against its own usual level of the past three months.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size the Monday bet against Sunday's move by how volatile the coin is against its own recent norm, and refuse it when volatility is low.
ideas.name: Sunday reversal in volatility

ideas.idea: A coin rises over the two hours ending 23:00 UTC. The rise is larger the higher the coin's current 30-day usual move stands against its own usual level of the past three months, and the further the coin fell over the previous 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: A trader would favour longs held through the late-evening UTC hours after a falling day in a volatile market, and refuse shorts held over them.
ideas.name: late-evening rise after falls
